newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases to 10.5 vs 11.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases to 10.5 vs 11.7 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate eased to 10.5 percent on Friday from 11.7 percent in lively but well balanced trade, dealers said.
Banks sought a total of 53.16 million kuna, of which 40 million in fresh loans. Supply stood at 58 million.
Interbank call money loans at around 10.5 percent accounted for most of the fresh borrowings. Term rates ranged between 11 and 15 percent.
Insurers rolled over old one-week loans at 9.0 percent.

The central bank stayed out of the market after intervening on Thursday by mopping up excess liquidity through a foreign exchange sale to commercial banks. It had also bought 1.0 million German marks at an average rate of 4.5625 kuna.
The kuna midrates for Saturday and next Monday firmed to 5.8189 versus 5.8452 against the dollar and to 3.5610 versus 3.5633 against the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
